lessonRef.title: Launch and diagnostic: why shared spaces need care

standardsRefs: Ready for Life v1, Grade 4 Unit 1: Home Care Routines That Last
Manuel Academy local Ready for Life composition
objective: I can practice why shared spaces need care. I will do one step at a time and check one result.
scenario: Every household has at least one space more than one person uses regularly, such as a kitchen table, a bathroom, or an entryway.
materials: learner-local: paper or a notes app
adult-or-local: one real shared space to observe in the learner's household

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u01-l01-model-card. Watch one complete example.

prompts.text: Name the first move in the model and explain why it comes first.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u01-l01-guided-card. Do the coached move.

prompts.text: Name the move you completed and the success check it meets.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u01-l01-independent-card. Choose one complete route. Follow its steps.

prompts.text: Which complete route did you use?
Record the completed step numbers and one non-sensitive result statement.

tasks.directions: Open swk-rfl-g4-u01-l01-evidence-record. Save one result and one reflection.

prompts.text: Name one specific thing you could do this week to help keep the shared space usable for everyone, and predict how at least one other person who shares that space would notice the difference.

remediation: Compare the missed move with the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l01-model-card; name one observable difference and review only the matching instruction step. Complete the affected move on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l01-guided-card with one coach prompt and receive feedback tied to the success check. Name the observable move that now meets the check and the one move, if any, that still needs correction. Do not use shame, trait, effort, or character judgments. Complete the same move on the fresh parallel condition in swk-rfl-g4-u01-l01-retry-pair without the coach prompt. Exit: The supported and parallel moves both meet the named success check: Shared-space reasoning: Explanation names at least one specific person besides the learner and how the space's condition affects that person. | Observation specificity: A specific recent moment is described with a concrete detail about what was cluttered, blocked, or missing. Resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l01-independent-card. A physical task resumes only with required permission and supervision; otherwise finish the equal-credit fictional route.
extension: Have the learner repeat the comparison for a second shared space used by a different group of people, such as a shared bathroom instead of a kitchen table, and explain which of the two spaces has a bigger effect on others when it is neglected, and why.

resources.title: why shared spaces need care worked model
resources.purpose: Shows the starting condition, visible moves, reasoning, and success check before the learner begins.
content: Starting condition: Every household has at least one space more than one person uses regularly, such as a kitchen table, a bathroom, or an entryway.
Model move 1: Read the condition and name the exact why shared spaces need care decision or action.
Model move 2: Walk through your household and pick one space that at least two people use regularly.
Model move 3: Look closely at the shared space as it is right now and think about a specific recent time it was cluttered, dirty, or hard to use.

Model check: Shared-space reasoning: Explanation names at least one specific person besides the learner and how the space's condition affects that person. | Observation specificity: A specific recent moment is described with a concrete detail about what was cluttered, blocked, or missing.

2. Watch the worked move on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l01-model-card.

resources.title: why shared spaces need care coached first attempt
resources.purpose: Carries the complete first attempt and a fresh correction turn.
content: Fictional practice condition: Every household has at least one space more than one person uses regularly, such as a kitchen table, a bathroom, or an entryway.
Coach direction: Walk through your household and pick one space that at least two people use regularly.
Learner prompt: Name the shared space you picked and list every person who regularly uses it.
Feedback check: name the move completed, point to the matching success check, and identify one missing or uncertain step without judging the learner.
Fresh correction turn: use the same fictional condition with one constraint changed; restate the changed constraint, redo only the affected step, and check the new result.

resources.title: why shared spaces need care complete application
resources.purpose: Contains the lesson-specific application directions and prompts; it is the delivered card referenced by the learner flow.
content: Application direction: Look closely at the shared space as it is right now and think about a specific recent time it was cluttered, dirty, or hard to use.
Response 1 (t2-p1): I named a specific recent moment the shared space was hard to use, not just a general feeling.
Response 2 (t2-p2): I identified at least one person besides myself who was affected by that moment.
Response 3 (t2-p3): I noted what specifically made the space hard to use, such as clutter, dirt, a missing item, or a blocked path.
Equal-access rule: Use the fictional condition above and complete the same reasoning and evidence without private real-world details.

resources.title: why shared spaces need care minimal evidence record
resources.purpose: Defines exactly what the learner saves and what must not be collected.
content: Record only: selected route, completed step numbers, one non-sensitive result statement, and one revision if a step changed.

Reflection: Name one specific thing you could do this week to help keep the shared space usable for everyone, and predict how at least one other person who shares that space would notice the difference.

Success checks: Shared-space reasoning: Explanation names at least one specific person besides the learner and how the space's condition affects that person. | Observation specificity: A specific recent moment is described with a concrete detail about what was cluttered, blocked, or missing.
Do not collect: names, signatures, addresses, or exact locations; account, identification, medical, product, or medicine details; photos, audio, video, passwords, or private household schedules.

resources.title: why shared spaces need care supported and parallel retry cards
resources.purpose: Delivers a real correction loop rather than a direction to try again without support.
content: Contrast reteach: compare the model check on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l01-model-card with the missed or unsupported step; name the one observable difference.
Supported card: return to swk-rfl-g4-u01-l01-guided-card, complete the affected move with one coach prompt, and receive criterion-specific feedback.
Parallel card: use a fresh fictional why shared spaces need care condition with one changed constraint; complete the same move without the coach prompt.

Exit check: the corrected move meets this lesson's checks — Shared-space reasoning: Explanation names at least one specific person besides the learner and how the space's condition affects that person. | Observation specificity: A specific recent moment is described with a concrete detail about what was cluttered, blocked, or missing..
Return: resume at the next unfinished step on swk-rfl-g4-u01-l01-independent-card; a physical route resumes only when the authorized adult says it is safe.

guardianInvolvement.role: Optional coach only; no guardian attestation is required.
guardianInvolvement.signOffBoundary: A guardian attestation certifies only that the named physical event occurred. It never scores the learner reflection or proves effort, honesty, maturity, responsibility, diagnosis, or character.

safety.stopRule: Stop the physical route when permission, supervision, a safe setting, or an expected material is missing, or when a new hazard appears. Continue only when the authorized adult resolves it; otherwise use the complete fictional route.
safety.physicalBoundary: The learner follows the source safety notes and never performs adult-only handling, transport, account, legal, medical, heat, sharp-tool, electrical, chemical, or machine actions.
safety.noShameRule: Describe only the observable step, condition, evidence, or revision. Never label the learner, household, body, ability, effort, maturity, responsibility, or character.

privacy.rule: Collect the smallest process record that shows the lesson steps. A learner may choose fictional details and may decline private disclosure without losing credit.

may: coach the guided and retry cards
mayNot: observe or claim a physical condition
tutorBoundary.physicalCompletionRule: Tutor or AI may coach. Tutor or AI may not certify that a real-world physical action occurred.
tutorBoundary.missingResourceAction: Stop and name the unresolved resource. Do not fabricate it; use another complete delivered route only when every resource for that route resolves.
